explanation: parse() must open with the def line, then try, then the conversion inside try, and only after the conversion can the except clause follow — the handler must reference the exception type before its own body. Putting the `return 0` fallback before the except line would attach it to the wrong clause. When the conversion raises, control jumps into the except body and returns 0.
prompt: Drag these lines into the order that makes parse('abc') return 0 instead of raising.
